idiom_name: distinct incomplete struct types used only through pointers
implementation_notes: C has no interfaces, no subtyping and no run-time type information; the nearest realization of a compile-time marker is a distinct incomplete struct type used only through pointers - typedef struct deletable deletable; makes deletable * incompatible with every other handle, so a marking API's parameter list enforces the category at zero runtime cost. The definition of struct deletable stays private to the implementation file, which also gives encapsulation. Use it to stop one handle being passed where another is expected; it cannot be tested at run time, because there is nothing to test.
pitfalls: A distinct opaque type only types the pointer; once a handle is cast to void * or stored in a common struct, the mark is gone - C has no instanceof.
Empty structs (struct marker {}) are a GCC extension, not ISO C; an incomplete type or a single char dummy member is the portable form.
Two opaque typedefs are unrelated even when their backing struct is the same, so the compiler cannot detect a mistaken cast between them.

variants.name: Tagged struct with an explicit discriminant
variants.idiom_name: enum discriminant in the common header struct, tested with a switch
variants.implementation_notes: When the category must be tested at run time, store an enum discriminant in the common header struct and switch on it; the mark becomes data that ordinary code checks, and the consumer is an ordinary function or switch. This is the C translation of a run-time type test, and it works with heterogeneous entities behind one struct layout. Nothing enforces consistency, so the discriminant must be set correctly at construction and kept in sync with any behaviour that depends on it.
pitfalls: The discriminant is plain data: nothing prevents constructing a struct with the wrong kind or mutating it later.
Every consumer switch needs a default branch, and adding a new kind silently falls through older switches.
Tag values are shared in one enum, so unrelated modules must agree on the numeric values or use named constants in a common header.

variants.name: Compile-time dispatch with _Generic
variants.idiom_name: _Generic selection on the controlling expression's type
variants.implementation_notes: C11 _Generic selects an expression by the type of its controlling expression at compile time, playing the role of C++ tag dispatch and making the mark a compile-time decision with no run-time tag storage. It dispatches on value types such as structs and integers, not on the pointee type of a handle, so it fits value-level markers and type-directed formatting or conversion helpers. Where the mark must survive as data, fall back to the tagged struct form.
variants.code_sketch:
#define kind_of(x) _Generic((x), \
    struct widget: KIND_WIDGET, struct gadget: KIND_GADGET, default: KIND_UNKNOWN)
pitfalls: _Generic requires an association for every type you intend to accept; an unlisted type silently takes the default branch instead of failing to compile.
It dispatches on the expression's type after lvalue conversions, so qualifiers and arrays can change which association matches.
It cannot inspect a pointer's target type - two opaque handle types look the same to _Generic.
